reasons: Covers the constructor, the single call, cycles and calibration with direct assertions.
A few checks are loose, but they still fail on the main breaks.

terms.meaning: A step that combines results from many items into one answer, here the portfolio reconciliation.
The component that checks processes against each other and adjusts scores.
A fake model connection that returns preset answers, so tests run without a real model.
A loop in prerequisites, where A needs B and B needs A, so work can never be scheduled.
A recorded change to a score, kept beside the original raw score.

used_by: Run by pytest. No importing file is visible.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and the rule being tested
sections.what: Brings in the reduce module, the reconciler types and the test helpers. The module docstring says an unreconciled portfolio must not be buildable.
sections.why: The docstring states the rule that these tests enforce.

sections.name: anyio_backend
sections.title: Run async tests on asyncio
sections.what: Tells the async test support to run these tests on Python's asyncio engine.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the choice of engine.

sections.name: edge
sections.title: Build one prerequisite link
sections.what: Creates a simple prerequisite link from one process to another, with a fixed reason and no evidence, for use as test data.
sections.why: Likely reason: many tests need a dependency graph, and building one inline each time would repeat code.

sections.name: output
sections.title: Build a fake reconciler answer
sections.what: Creates the reconciler's typed output from the given links and adjustments, with no capacity findings.
sections.why: Lets tests control exactly what the model appears to return, without calling a model.

sections.name: records
sections.title: Build test process records
sections.what: Creates process records with a fixed enabler and effort, so each test has the same kind of input.
sections.why: Likely reason: a shared builder keeps test inputs identical from one test to the next.

sections.name: empty_result
sections.title: Build an empty reconciliation result
sections.what: Creates a reconciliation result with no adjustments, links or cycles, and with the capacity check marked as not run.
sections.why: Used where a portfolio is needed but the reconciliation content does not matter to the test.

sections.name: TestAPortfolioCannotSkipTheReduce
sections.title: Only the reduce can make a portfolio
sections.what: Checks that reconciliation is required to build a portfolio, that only the reconcile function is annotated to return one, that the reduce takes a collection, that a single record is refused, and that a portfolio of one is refused even with a reconciliation.
sections.why: The docstring says the rule is enforced by the constructor signature rather than by a comment, so it cannot be skipped by accident.
sections.watch_out: The producer check reads return annotations. A function that returns a portfolio without an annotation would not be found.

sections.name: TestItRunsOnceOverEverything
sections.title: Reduce runs once over everything
sections.what: Checks that the reconciler sees every record in a single model call, that exactly one call is made, and that the records come back unchanged.
sections.why: The reduce is designed to look at the whole portfolio at once, so the tests check that it does.
sections.watch_out: The check that every record reaches the reconciler looks for single letters inside the message text, which can match unrelated words.

sections.name: TestCycles
sections.title: Cycles stop the portfolio
sections.what: Checks that a loop in prerequisites raises an error that names the loop, that the loop can be inspected when explicitly allowed, and that a graph with no loop passes.
sections.why: Likely reason: a loop means the work can never be scheduled, so the portfolio is refused.
sections.watch_out: The error check matches exact wording and the order of the loop, so rewording the error breaks it.

sections.name: TestCalibrationIsAdditiveAndRawScoresStayFrozen
sections.title: Calibration changes the score, not the original
sections.what: Checks that an adjustment changes the calibrated score while the raw score stays as the author wrote it, that untouched dimensions read raw, that an unknown dimension raises a key error, and that an adjustment naming a process outside the portfolio is refused.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeping the raw score lets a reader see what the author said and how it was changed.
sections.watch_out: The calibrated score for an unknown dimension depends on the exact error message wording.

sections.name: TestTheReduceIsNotReachablePerProcess
sections.title: Reduce does not import the pipeline
sections.what: Checks that the reduce module does not import the per-process pipeline module.
sections.why: The docstring says the rule goes one way only. If the reduce imported the pipeline, a loop could expose the reconciler to a per-process call by accident.
sections.watch_out: Only checks direct imports. An indirect route through another module would not be caught.

summary: Checks that a portfolio can only be built by the reduce step, that the reduce makes one model call over all records, and that cycle and calibration rules hold.
purpose: Protects the portfolio-level step. A portfolio that was never reconciled must not be buildable, and the reduce must see everything at once.
why: The module docstring states the rule directly. The file tests it through the constructor and the function signatures so the rule holds in code, not only in documentation.
how: The file builds small fake records, fake reconciler outputs and empty results. It then checks the constructor refuses unreconciled or too-small portfolios, that the reconcile function is the only one annotated to return a portfolio, that one model call sees every record, that cycles stop the portfolio unless allowed, and that calibration adds to raw scores without changing them.
inputs: Fake process records, fake reconciler outputs and a stub model client built in the shared fixtures module. No live model or network calls.
outputs: Pass or fail results from pytest.
risks: Some checks are loose. The check that every record reaches the reconciler searches message text for single letters, which can match unrelated text. The producer check reads return annotations, so an unannotated producer would be missed.
debug: If a test fails, open packages/orchestration/reduce.py and check the Portfolio constructor and reconcile_portfolio. For cycle failures, look at the prerequisite edges the stub returns. For calibration failures, check calibrated_score.
